item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-28 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

This project investigates how sleep impairments disrupt the brain's glymphatic system, which clears metabolic waste during deep sleep, thereby promoting the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and tau proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD). It aims to address a critical knowledge gap in how impaired glymphatic clearance, interacting with broader AD risk factors, predicts clinical onset and disease progression, with a specific focus on cortical hyperexcitability and subclinical epileptiform activity detected via resting-state EEG (rsEEG) and linked to accelerated cognitive decline
